**[American Sign Language](/wiki/American_Sign_Language "American Sign Language")** (ASL) is the native language of a number of [deaf](/wiki/Deaf "Deaf") and hearing people in America (roughly 100,000 to 500,000). While some sources have stated that ASL is the third most frequently used language in the United States, after English and Spanish,[[134]](#cite_note-preston1995p243-138) recent scholarship has pointed out that most of these estimates are based on numbers conflating deafness with ASL use, and that the last actual study of this (in 1972) seems to indicate an upper bound of 500,000 ASL speakers at the time.[[135]](#cite_note-gallaudet2006-139)

* [Black American Sign Language](/wiki/Black_American_Sign_Language "Black American Sign Language") (BASL) developed in the southeastern United States, where separate residential schools were maintained for white and black deaf children. BASL shares much of the same vocabulary and grammatical structure as ASL and is generally considered one of its dialects.[[133]](#cite_note-EthnologueASL-137)[[134]](#cite_note-preston1995p243-138)[[136]](#cite_note-140)

**[Hawaiʻi Sign Language](/wiki/Hawai%CA%BBi_Sign_Language "Hawaiʻi Sign Language")** is moribund with only a handful of speakers on [Oʻahu](/wiki/O%CA%BBahu "Oʻahu"), [Lānaʻi](/wiki/L%C4%81na%CA%BBi "Lānaʻi"), [Kauaʻi](/wiki/Kaua%CA%BBi "Kauaʻi") and possibly [Niʻihau](/wiki/Ni%CA%BBihau "Niʻihau"). Some of these speakers may actually be speaking a creolized version of HSL and ASL, however; research is slow-going. The language was once called Hawaiʻi Pidgin Sign Language, as many people thought it was a derivative of ASL, but it was discovered to be a separate language altogether.[[137]](#cite_note-LambrechtEarthWoodward-141)

Despite considerable losses, in early 1942 Germany and its allies stopped a major Soviet offensive in [central](/wiki/Central_Russia "Central Russia") and [southern Russia](/wiki/Southern_Russia "Southern Russia"), keeping most territorial gains they had achieved during the previous year.[[220]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGlantz200131-223) In May, the Germans defeated Soviet offensives in the [Kerch Peninsula](/wiki/Battle_of_the_Kerch_Peninsula "Battle of the Kerch Peninsula") and at [Kharkov](/wiki/Second_Battle_of_Kharkov "Second Battle of Kharkov").[[221]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTERead2004764-224) The fortress city of Sevastopol, which the Red Army had held out against Axis siege for nearly 250 days, was finally seized with the use of massive artillery bombardments and poison gas.[[222]](#cite_note-225)

In June 1942 Germany launched its main [summer offensive](/wiki/Case_Blue "Case Blue") against southern Russia, to seize the [oil fields of the Caucasus](/wiki/Petroleum_industry_in_Azerbaijan "Petroleum industry in Azerbaijan") and occupy the [Kuban](/wiki/Kuban "Kuban") [steppe](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe"), while maintaining positions on the northern and central areas of the front. The Germans split [Army Group South](/wiki/Army_Group_South "Army Group South") into two groups: [Army Group A](/wiki/Army_Group_A "Army Group A") advanced to the lower [Don River](/wiki/Don_(river) "Don (river)") and struck south-east to the Caucasus, while [Army Group B](/wiki/Army_Group_B "Army Group B") headed towards the [Volga River](/wiki/Volga "Volga"). The Soviet Union decided to make its stand at Stalingrad on the Volga.[[223]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDavies2006p._100_(2008_ed.)-226)

Federal regions also have their own departments of health that oversee local administration. A separate private health insurance plan is needed to access private healthcare in Russia.[[83]](#cite_note-86)

Russia spent 5.32% of its GDP on healthcare in 2018.[[84]](#cite_note-87) Its healthcare expenditure is notably lower than other developed nations.[[85]](#cite_note-88) Russia has one of the world's most female-biased [sex ratios](/wiki/Human_sex_ratio "Human sex ratio"), with 0.859 males to every female with more older females than males prevailing,[[86]](#cite_note-cia-89) due to its high male [mortality rate](/wiki/Mortality_rate "Mortality rate") in later age.[[87]](#cite_note-90) In 2019, the overall [life expectancy in Russia](/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy "List of countries by life expectancy") at birth was 73.2 years (68.2 years for males and 78.0 years for females),[[88]](#cite_note-91) and it had a very low [infant mortality rate](/wiki/Infant_mortality "Infant mortality") (5 per 1,000 [live births](/wiki/Live_birth_(human) "Live birth (human)")).[[89]](#cite_note-92)

Sémillon, which is relatively easy to cultivate,[[3]](#cite_note-oxf-sem-3) consistently produces six to eight tons of grapes per acre from its vigorous vines.[[4]](#cite_note-pro-4) It is fairly resistant to disease, except for rot. The grape ripens early, when, in warmer climates, it acquires a pinkish hue.[[5]](#cite_note-cork-5) Since the grape has a thin skin, there is also a risk of sunburn in hotter climates; it is best suited to areas with sunny days and cool nights.

Sémillon wines are rather heavy, with low acidity and an almost oily texture. It has a high yield and wines based on it can age a long time. Along with [Sauvignon blanc](/wiki/Sauvignon_blanc "Sauvignon blanc") and [Muscadelle](/wiki/Muscadelle "Muscadelle"), Sémillon is one of only three approved white wine varieties in the [Bordeaux region](/wiki/Bordeaux_wine "Bordeaux wine").

The grape is also key to the production of sweet wines such as [Sauternes](/wiki/Sauternes_(wine) "Sauternes (wine)"). For the grapes to be used for sweet wine production, they need to have been affected by [Botrytis](/wiki/Botrytis_cinerea "Botrytis cinerea") (also known as "[noble rot](/wiki/Noble_rot "Noble rot")"). This fungus dries out the grapes, thus concentrating the sugar and flavours in the grape berry.

The **Maldives**,[[c]](#cite_note-10) officially the **Republic of Maldives**,[[d]](#cite_note-11) and historically known as the **Maldive Islands**, is an [archipelagic country](/wiki/Archipelagic_state "Archipelagic state") in [South Asia](/wiki/South_Asia "South Asia"), located in the [Indian Ocean](/wiki/Indian_Ocean "Indian Ocean"), near the southeastern boundary of the [Arabian Sea](/wiki/Arabian_Sea "Arabian Sea"). The Maldives is located in the southwest of [India](/wiki/India "India") and [Sri Lanka](/wiki/Sri_Lanka "Sri Lanka"), about 750 kilometres (470 miles; 400 nautical miles) from the Asian continent's mainland. The Maldives' chain of [26 atolls](/wiki/Atolls_of_the_Maldives "Atolls of the Maldives") stretches across the equator from [Ihavandhippolhu Atoll](/wiki/Atolls_of_the_Maldives#Ihavandhippolhu "Atolls of the Maldives") in the north to [Addu Atoll](/wiki/Seenu_Atoll "Seenu Atoll") in the south.

The Maldives is the smallest [country in Asia](/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states_and_dependent_territories_in_Asia "List of sovereign states and dependent territories in Asia"). Its land area is only 298 square kilometres (115 sq mi), but this is spread over roughly 90,000 square kilometres (35,000 sq mi) of the sea, making it one of the world's most spatially dispersed sovereign states. With a population of 515,132 in the 2022 census, it is the second [least populous country in Asia](/wiki/List_of_Asian_countries_by_population "List of Asian countries by population") and the [ninth-smallest country by area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area"), but also one of the [most densely populated countries](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population_density "List of countries and dependencies by population density").
